sourceEvidence.claim: The Apoptosis definition block — ATP-dependent programmed cell death; caspases; shrinkage/condensation/blebbing/apoptotic bodies phagocytosed; eosinophilic cytoplasm and basophilic nucleus; pyknosis and karyorrhexis; intact membrane without significant inflammation (unlike necrosis); DNA laddering at 180 bp
sourceEvidence.quote:
ATP-dependent programmed cell death.
Intrinsic, extrinsic, and perforin/granzyme B pathways → activate caspases (cytosolic proteases)
→ cellular breakdown including cell shrinkage, chromatin condensation, membrane blebbing,
and formation of apoptotic bodies, which are then phagocytosed.
Characterized by deeply eosinophilic cytoplasm and basophilic nucleus, pyknosis, and karyorrhexis.
Cell membrane typically remains intact without significant inflammation (unlike necrosis).
DNA laddering (fragments in multiples of 180 bp) is a sensitive indicator of apoptosis.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: Intrinsic pathway triggers — embryogenesis tissue remodeling; IL-2 withdrawal after a completed immunologic reaction; radiation, toxins, hypoxia
sourceEvidence.quote:
Intrinsic
(mitochondrial)
pathway

Involved in tissue remodeling in embryogenesis. Occurs when a regulating factor is withdrawn
from a proliferating cell population (eg, ↓ IL-2 after a completed immunologic reaction
→ apoptosis of proliferating effector cells). Also occurs after exposure to injurious stimuli (eg,
radiation, toxins, hypoxia).

sourceEvidence.claim: The Bcl-2 rheostat with the source's own inline mnemonics — 'Bad for survival' and 'Be clever, live'
sourceEvidence.quote:
Regulated by Bcl-2 family of proteins. Bax and Bak are proapoptotic (Bad for survival), while Bcl-2
and Bcl-xL are antiapoptotic (Be clever, live).

sourceEvidence.claim: The intrinsic mechanism and the jammed door — BAX/BAK pores, cytochrome C release, caspase activation; Bcl-2 impermeability; follicular lymphoma t(14;18) overexpression → tumorigenesis
sourceEvidence.quote:
BAX and BAK form pores in the outer mitochondrial membrane → release of cytochrome C from
the mitochondrial intermembrane space into the cytoplasm → activation of caspases.
Bcl-2 keeps the mitochondrial membrane impermeable, thereby preventing cytochrome C release.
Bcl-2 overexpression (eg, follicular lymphoma t[14;18]) → ↓ caspase activation → tumorigenesis.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The extrinsic pathway — FasL-Fas (CD95), TNF-α-TNFR; thymic medullary negative selection; autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome (failure of clonal deletion, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, autoimmune cytopenias)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Extrinsic (death
receptor) pathway

Ligand receptor interactions: FasL binding to Fas (CD95) or TNF-α binding to its receptor.
Fas-FasL interaction is necessary in thymic medullary negative selection.
Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome—caused by defective Fas-FasL interaction → failure
of clonal deletion → ↑ numbers of self-reacting lymphocytes. Presents with lymphadenopathy,
hepatosplenomegaly, autoimmune cytopenias.

sourceEvidence.claim: The perforin/granzyme B pathway — cytotoxic T-cell and NK-cell granules; perforin forms the pore
sourceEvidence.quote:
Perforin/granzyme B
pathway

Release of granules containing perforin and granzyme B by immune cells (cytotoxic T-cell and
natural killer cell) → perforin forms a pore for granzyme B to enter the target cell.
